reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended The `pwsh` executor bypasses shared PowerShell setup, dropping execution options and error/exit-code handling that affect command behavior and reported results.
1 open issue - [Apply PowerShell setup when using pwsh](https://github.com/OpenAEV-Platform/implant/pull/227#discussion_r4674096221) · New
What changed in this PR This PR addresses #73 by preferring PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) for implant payload execution when available, while retaining Windows PowerShell as the fallback. **Changes:** - Adds a shared helper for selecting `pwsh`. - Uses the helper for PSH commands and Windows file execution. - Adds tests for interpreter selection and fallback behavior. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `src/​tests/​process/​command_exec_tests.rs` | Tests `pwsh` selection and fallback behavior. | | `src/​process/​file_exec.rs` | Prefers `pwsh` for Windows file execution. | | `src/​process/​exec_utils.rs` | Adds the shared `prefer_pwsh` helper. | | `src/​process/​command_exec.rs` | Applies interpreter selection to Windows and Unix PSH commands. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: Selecting `pwsh` bypasses the PowerShell setup in `command_execution`, which only checks `final_executor == EXECUTOR_POWERSHELL`. Payloads then lose the no-profile/noninteractive options, execution-policy bypass, and wrapper that stops on errors and propagates `$LASTEXITCODE`, changing execution and reported results. Update that shared condition at line 117 to recognize `pwsh` too; the Unix mapping at line 70 has the same issue.
